title: 결제 3칸 포켓
oneLiner: 여행 전 세 곳을 골라 카드·교통카드·현금의 주·백업·비상 순서를 실제 실패 장면으로 익히고 오프라인 포켓카드로 가져가는 결제 리허설.
theme: 자산 방어 — prevent payment panic and unnecessary cash exposure.
targetUser: first-time Korea visitors, exchange students, older travelers, and hotels onboarding guests.
keyUX: choose three upcoming stops, arrange payment tools, flip failure scenarios, correct the sequence, then download a minimal offline card with exact fallback order and Korean help phrases.

sourceSignals.note: Traveler payment panic and improvised card, cash, and transit backups.

format: interactive rehearsal plus printable/offline wallet card.
mechanic: drag payment tools into Primary, Backup, and Emergency pockets, then survive three realistic failure cards.
triggerMoment: the traveler is packing and cannot tell which payment method works where.
buyerShareAudience: travelers, hotels, airlines, tour operators, and travel insurers.
userActionSentence: “카드가 안 되면 뭘 먼저 꺼내야 하는지 출국 전에 알고 싶어요.”
threeSecondSting: a subway gate rejects the foreign card while three empty pockets ask “다음 수단은?”
outputArtifact: bilingual offline three-pocket payment card tied to three planned stops.
firstValidationTest: test 15 visitors on subway, convenience-store, and small-market scenarios; measure correct fallback selection and cash over-carry intention.
lovedBySmallGroup: 4/5 — first-time visitors with foreign cards and tightly budgeted itineraries fear being stranded at transit gates.
smallGroupFit: visitors who have never used Korean transit can validate value before landing.
spreadTrigger: a bilingual three-pocket card can be saved offline and forwarded to travel companions.
referencePattern: emergency go-bag + card-game rehearsal + travel phrase card.
twist: it teaches action order through failure instead of comparing payment products in a static article.
firstScreen: one rejected subway gate, three empty pockets, and the traveler's actual next three stops.
shareOrPlayLoop: rehearse → save card → share with companion → mark which fallback actually worked → update the card.
planBrief: User problem: payment knowledge is fragmented by place and top-up method. Inflow: trip confirmation or community search. Business: hotel/tour onboarding kit. Core loop: choose stops → place tools → face failures → correct → save offline. First screen: a failed gate, not a comparison table. Interaction rules: no claim that a card is universally accepted; always show observation date and cash safety. QA: no NFC phone, no airport kiosk, empty transit balance, lost card, offline state, two languages, large text. Risk: acceptance rules change.
developmentStartPrompt: Build a mobile travel rehearsal with three mocked destinations, draggable payment methods, Primary/Backup/Emergency pockets, failure flips, corrective feedback, Korean help phrases, and an offline card preview. Keep acceptance claims caveated and dated.
stitchPrompt: Create a mobile-first Korea travel companion called “결제 3칸 포켓” for first-time visitors who are panicking over T-money, WOWPASS, foreign cards, cash, and airport-only top-up rules. Start at a subway gate that rejects a foreign card; beside it are three empty pockets labeled 주수단, 백업, 비상. Let the traveler choose their next three stops—a subway gate, convenience store, and small market—then drag their real payment tools into the pockets. Flip realistic failure cards one at a time, explain only the next safe action, and let the traveler correct the order. Finish with a bilingual offline wallet card containing the three-stop sequence, top-up caveats, a conservative cash note, and Korean help phrases. Include no-NFC-phone, empty transit balance, lost card, closed kiosk, and companion-share states. Required sections: stops, tool tray, three pockets, failure cards, correction, caveats, phrase strip, offline card, and share. Emotional pressure: being stranded or exposing too much cash. Design direction: use the calm-consumer profile with warm white and pale sage surfaces, one clear teal accent, large friendly pockets, 48px drag targets, explicit offline state, and no fintech charts, product ranking, or glossy travel hero.
